runbook_walk.script:
# 1. No backup during the restore: both CronJobs suspended, and any backup Job still running left to finish.
for c in ospreyflow-backup ospreyflow-backup-claims; do
  kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev patch cronjob "$c" -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' 2>/dev/null
done
kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev get jobs -l 'app.kubernetes.io/name in (backup,backup-claims)'   # none still Running
# 2. Note each copy count, then stop everything that writes and wait for its pods to be gone (a finished
#    backup Job's pods are kept, and are not waited for: they run nothing).
W=$(python3 -c 'import sys, yaml; print(",".join(yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))["backups"]["writers"]))' /root/osprey-runs/case.tools/render/values.yaml)
kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev get deployment,statefulset -l "app.kubernetes.io/name in ($W)" \
  -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,COPIES:.spec.replicas
kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev scale deployment,statefulset -l "app.kubernetes.io/name in ($W)" --replicas=0
kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev wait --for=delete pod -l "app.kubernetes.io/name in ($W),!job-name" --timeout=10m
#    Now the platform team points the namespace's database settings at the RDS instance restored above
#    (its Terraform), and it is available, before step 3.
# 3. The restore's Jobs, rendered for the set by its own name (never `latest`; never by `helm upgrade`,
#    which would start ArcadeDB); a Job of the same name from an earlier attempt removed first.
kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev delete job -l 'app.kubernetes.io/name in (restore,restore-claims)' --ignore-not-found --wait
helm template ospreyflow deploy/helm/ospreyflow -n ospreyflow-dev -f /root/osprey-runs/case.tools/render/values.yaml \
  --set backups.restore.set=20261112T034000Z --show-only templates/backups.yaml \
  | kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev apply -f - --selector='app.kubernetes.io/name in (restore,restore-claims)'
for j in $(kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev get jobs -l 'app.kubernetes.io/name in (restore,restore-claims)' -o name); do
  kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.conditions[0].status}'=True "$j" --timeout=6h
  kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev logs "$j" --all-containers | tail -3     # each step says what it did, or why not
  kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev get "$j" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' | grep -qx 1 \
    || { echo "$j did not finish: start nothing; read its log (below, If it fails)"; break; }
done
# 4. Only when every Job finished: start each again at the copy count noted in step 2, ArcadeDB first,
#    then the backups resumed.
kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev scale statefulset/arcadedb --replicas=1
kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev rollout status statefulset/arcadedb
kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev scale deployment/api --replicas=1
for c in ospreyflow-backup ospreyflow-backup-claims; do
  kubectl -n ospreyflow-dev patch cronjob "$c" -p '{"spec":{"suspend":false}}' 2>/dev/null
done
